sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2022. Comprehensive Bibliography of Chadic and Hausa Linguistics, 5th ed. Bloomington: IU ScholarWorks.
sources.note: Used to enumerate all Gidar-keyed items: Collard 1973 (noms-numéros), Frajzyngier 2003b/2005a/2008a/2010d/2013a, Frajzyngier-Krech-Mirzayan 2002, Frajzyngier & Shay 2008, Hagège 1974/1975/1979, Mayssal et al. 1967 (poetry), Nseme 2001 (gender), Schuh 1984a/2010. No item on Gidar stress or accent.

sources.citation: WALS Online (Dryer & Haspelmath eds. 2013), language gdr Gidar, source Frajzyngier-1996
sources.note: Gidar has a single WALS value and none in the stress chapters 14A-17A (Goedemans & van der Hulst).

sources.citation: Noukeu, Serge. 2002. Esquisse phonologique du Kada (Guidar). Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. iii+95 pp. (French)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: Whole thesis is phonology: Chap. I Les tons pp. 8-10 (two tonemes, haut and bas: 'C'est le cas de la langue Kada qui utilise la hauteur mélodique à des fins distinctives', p. 8), Part II distribution of tonemes in mono-/di-/trisyllables pp. 52-53 (all H/B combinations occur), orthography chapter with tone graphemes. No mention of stress, accent, or intensity anywhere (grep of scanned layer for accent/intensit/proémin/prosod: none). Open copy from MPI 'Language Description Heritage' REST endpoint (landing page bot-gated).

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1984. Données de la langue kaɗa (gidar). Ms., Ahmadu Bello University Zaria / UCLA. 90 pp. (French)
sources.note: §2 Phonologie (pp. 6-19), §2.2.3 Tons p. 11: 'Le gidar n'a que deux tons au niveau phonématique, haut (H) et bas (B)', plus a falling tone analysed as H+B; nothing on stress or accent. Chapter 8 'Questions et Accentuation' (pp. 65 ff.) uses 'accentuation' for focus/emphasis of subject and object, not phonological stress; 8.1 notes no marked intonation difference between declaratives and yes/no questions. Wayback copy of the UCLA PDF (host now 404).
